name: quick_cache (S3-FIFO concurrent cache)
baseline: An LRU cache behind std::sync::Mutex (hashlink LruCache), and Mini Moka
verdict_reason: On the ARC traces it reaches 3x to 5.5x the hit ratio of a mutex-wrapped LRU at small capacities while costing about the same per operation single-threaded, and it scales with threads. It ran 2.6x to 4.3x faster than Mini Moka at similar hit ratios.
tier_reason: First-party run of the public mokabench harness with the CPU named, but no rustc version or flags.
claimed_speedup: ARC S3 trace, 100000 entries: hit ratio 12.841% vs 2.327% for LRU+Mutex; run time 2.196 s vs 2.422 s single client, 0.798 s with 6 clients; Mini Moka 9.399 s. ARC DS1, 1000000 entries: 14.864% vs 3.086% hit ratio, 9.883 s vs 8.901 s (slightly slower single-threaded).
workload: mokabench replaying ARC paper traces (S3 search, DS1 database, SPC1) with 1, 3 and 6 client threads; a miss triggers an insert; no simulated miss penalty.
platforms: Any Rust target; no background threads
one_liner: Sharded S3-FIFO cache: up to 5.5x the hit ratio of Mutex<LRU> at similar per-op cost, about 4x faster than Mini Moka.
how_it_is_fast: S3-FIFO keeps a small probationary queue and a main queue with a ghost list, so one-hit items are evicted early without the list reordering LRU needs on every hit. Shards with their own locks spread contention across threads, and there are no background maintenance threads.
use_it_when: A hand-rolled Mutex<LRU> or the lru crate shows a low hit ratio on scan-heavy or frequency-skewed access
skip_it_when: You need time-to-live, time-to-idle or per-entry expiry: moka has them, quick_cache does not
Single-threaded code with a cache that already holds the working set: a plain LRU was as fast
caveats: First-party run, September 2024, quick_cache 0.6; the crate is now 0.7
mokabench charges nothing for a miss, so hit-ratio gains show up only as fewer inserts, not as saved backend latency
tradeoffs: Fewer features than moka (no TTL, no eviction listener beyond lifecycle hooks)
Approximate eviction order per shard rather than strict global LRU

evidence.quote: Benchmarks performed with [mokabench](https://github.com/moka-rs/mokabench) in a x64 Linux OS + Intel i9-12900H CPU.
